[AlphaFold](https://deepmind.com/blog/article/putting-the-power-of-alphafold-into-the-worlds-hands) is an AI system developed by [Google DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/) that predicts a protein’s 3D structure from its amino acid sequence. Google DeepMind and EMBL’s European Bioinformatics Institute ([EMBL-EBI](http://www.ebi.ac.uk)) have partnered to create AlphaFold DB to make these predictions freely available to the scientific community. source_links.context: Today Anthropic launches [Claude Science](http://claude.com/product/claude-science), Anthropic’s AI workbench for scientists, where life sciences researchers can run computational workloads directly from a conversation with Claude - from data processing pipelines to structure prediction models to molecule design campaigns.

When that happens in Claude Science, researchers can connect their own Modal workspace. Workloads that require GPUs or many concurrent CPUs route to [Modal sandboxes](https://modal.com/docs/guide/sandboxes) automatically. The researcher stays in Claude. Modal handles the compute: bursty, heterogeneous workloads that outgrow any fixed cluster or single GPU type.

**GPU access per step.** Biology pipelines are rarely all-GPU or all-CPU. A typical workflow might do alignment and preprocessing on CPU, then hand off to [ESMFold2](https://modal.com/docs/examples/esmfold2) or a similar model for structure prediction on GPU. With Modal, you request a GPU for that one function, not for the whole pipeline.

**Shared storage across jobs.** Moving around things like sequencing datasets, protein databases, and model checkpoints between pipeline steps is expensive. With [Modal Volumes](https://modal.com/docs/guide/volumes), it's done once and available across every job, whether you're running one query or thousands.

**Reproducible environments.** [Modal Images](https://modal.com/docs/guide/images) make it easy to define and manage dependencies for each type of compute job, so environments are concise and consistent across runs. No surprises when someone else on the team tries to reproduce a result.

[Chai Discovery](https://modal.com/blog/seamless-computational-bio-at-chai-discovery) builds ML-driven drug discovery pipelines that chain together protein embeddings, multiple sequence alignments, and antibody design models, each step running on whatever hardware matches its compute shape.

1. Download the Claude Science app at [claude.com/science](http://claude.com/science) .
2. In Settings, navigate to the Compute configuration section.
3. Connect to your Modal workspace. If you don't have a Modal account yet, create one at [modal.com/signup](http://modal.com/signup) — it takes a few minutes and includes $30 in free compute to start.
4. Once connected, compute workloads will run on Modal automatically.

Trilogy built its [AI Cybersecurity Playbook](https://trilogyai.substack.com/p/ai-cybersecurity-playbook-kimi-k3) around Kimi K3 on Fireworks because defensive AI workloads require a deployment path that organizations can depend on.

The defender's workload is continuous. Teams audit repositories, triage scanner output, review pull requests, investigate alerts, and preserve incident timelines. During the recent Hugging Face incident, [frontier models breached production infrastructure](https://openai.com/index/hugging-face-model-evaluation-security-incident/) during an authorized evaluation and executed more than 17,000 autonomous actions over the course of multiple days, before containment. Due to the persistence and scale

The Trilogy AI Center of Excellence built a public AI Cybersecurity Playbook and exercise pack around Kimi K3 on Fireworks. Its [technical overview](https://trilogyai.substack.com/p/ai-cybersecurity-playbook-kimi-k3) links the interactive playbook, the repository, and ten exercises against local training applications.

Fireworks exposes Kimi K3 through an [OpenAI-compatible API](https://docs.fireworks.ai/tools-sdks/openai-compatibility), which lets teams integrate the model with familiar clients, agent frameworks, scanners, and CI systems.

With Kimi K3's weights public, teams have a broader deployment spectrum. They can begin with the [managed Fireworks endpoint](https://app.fireworks.ai/models/fireworks/kimi-k3) and evaluate dedicated capacity as volume, latency, or isolation requirements grow. The surrounding audit workflow remains under the team's control while Fireworks operates the model-serving infrastructure.

Sycophantic systems that tell users what they want to hear, overreliance on AI, loss of skills, mental-health effects and labor-market disruption can all diminish human agency. Those harms do not come with an obvious off switch.

Reich said the incentives inside a race dynamic cut against any slowdown. If it hasn't occurred to them that a one-day withdrawal of labor might signal how serious this is, “then I'm not sure I take the whole letter seriously i

He added that Sam Altman has his job because during the OpenAI board crisis, employees declared the company was nothing without them. “It was labor organizing that saved Sam Altman's job. Labor organizing, in this ordinary sense, can also be very consequential across labs to try to pace the frontier.”

AgentENV targets exactly that gap. It runs [Firecracker](https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker) microVMs, then makes idle, restart, and branching cheap enough to run at training scale.

Storage is where the design gets interesting. The rootfs is served through a **ublk** userspace block device backed by **[overlaybd](https://github.com/containerd/overlaybd)** layered images. Read-only base layers are shared across sandboxes, and each sandbox writes into its own upper layer.

source_links.context: That is the central finding from a [new survey of 1,039 GitHub users](https://climatecommunication.yale.edu/publications/github-survey/) conducted by GitHub and the Yale Program on Climate Change Communication. Eight in 10 respondents said they were interested in tools that help them write more energy-efficient code. Nearly as many wanted best practices for reducing software’s environmental footprint, and almost 75% wanted ways to measure the impact of their software or development process.

The open source [Daily Efficiency Improver workflow](https://github.com/githubnext/agentics/blob/main/docs/efficiency-improver.md) reviews a repository for opportunities across code, data, network, I/O, and frontend performance. It prioritizes changes that can be measured, runs the repository’s tests, and can open draft pull requests with the evidence and trade-offs for maintainers to review. It does not merge changes itself.

His return didn’t quite stick. Zoph spent only five months at OpenAI, where he was tasked with heading AI enterprise sales. He [left the company](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/952837/barret-zoph-openai-thinking-machines-lab) in June. And now we know where he landed.

Zoph has taken a position as vice president of research at Google (which happens to be another company where he previously worked). “We look forward to Barret returning to Google and bringing his RL and post-training expertise to Gemini,” a Google spokesperson told the [Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/thinking-machines-lab-co-founder-barret-zoph-joins-google-49f594e6).

reader_metadata.author: Matthias Bastian
reader_metadata.description: Suno CEO Mikey Shulman has announced new guidelines and tighter download limits after its AI-generated music was used to game streaming platforms for profit. The company also faces pressure from a German copyright ruling and an admission by one of its investors that AI music competes directly with human artists.
reader_metadata.title: AI music generator Suno tightens rules to fight spam and address growing copyright concerns

A [German court recently ruled](https://the-decoder.de/landgericht-muenchen-verurteilt-ki-musikgenerator-suno-wegen-urheberrechtsverletzung/) that Suno used copyrighted songs during training and can reproduce them when prompted the right way. The court also found that the US fair use doctrine doesn't apply to Suno's case. Before that ruling, [one of Suno's own investors](https://the-decoder.de/suno-investorin-raeumt-ein-ki-musik-steht-in-direkter-konkurrenz-zu-menschlichen-kuenstlern/) admitted

Suno co-founder and CEO Mikey Shulman laid out four guiding principles and a set of new measures in a [blog post](https://suno.com/blog). The company says it follows a training strategy called "Original Creation, By Design" that's meant to reduce the risk of unauthorized reproductions. Specifically, Suno says it deliberately left artist names out of its training metadata.

The company also says it has never allowed prompts targeting specific artists or copyrighted songs. On top of that, Suno works with Audible Magic, [Musixmatch](https://sentinel.musixmatch.com/), and other third-party services to check uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential unauthorized use.

source_links.anchor: push songs onto streaming platforms in bulk
source_links.context: Suno acknowledges that its technology shouldn't be abused to export content at scale. Most music created on the platform is personal, the company says. Still, it's rolling out a new download policy designed to limit the ability to [push songs onto streaming platforms in bulk](https://the-decoder.com/the-flood-of-ai-music-is-reshaping-how-streaming-platforms-handle-new-uploads/).

source_links.anchor: In March, a man was convicted
source_links.context: Most users won't be affected, according to Suno, but large-scale abuse will become much harder. The company says it first announced such a step last year. [In March, a man was convicted](https://the-decoder.com/a-man-created-thousands-of-fake-accounts-to-stream-ai-songs-billions-of-times-and-pocket-8-million-in-royalties/) after uploading hundreds of thousands of songs made with AI and fraudulently collecting $8 million in royalties.

Alongside these changes, Suno says it has made its [community guidelines](https://suno.com/community-guidelines) more explicit. The company says it has always banned attempts to replicate existing songs, uploading material without proper rights, and using someone's voice or likeness without permission. Its rules also prohibit spam, fake engagement, bots, and deceptive audio presented as authentic.

A single *forward pass* through such a neural network produces both substantial internal state and a probability distribution over the next token(s) in the sequence for each sequence position. Because we predict ([”regress”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regression_toward_the_mean)) based on our own outputs (”auto”), this is *autoregressive* sequence modeling.

Forward passes are expensive, so we want to amortize this work as much as possible. Much of the work in per-token computation amortizes by *batching* several sequences together. Much of the work in cross-token computation amortizes by *caching* the internal state. For historical reasons, this is called the *key-value cache* (KV cache or just *KV*), even though contemporary models like Kimi don’t have distinct keys and values. source_links.context: Early adopters of Meta’s Muse have been speculating that the reason the AI works so well is because it’s OpenClaw under the hood, wrapped in a more consumer-friendly package. Meta now says those comparisons aren’t entirely off-base. According to an [X post](https://x.com/natfriedman/status/2102103707936768130) by Nat Friedman, head of product at Meta’s Superintelligence Labs (MSL), Muse was “definitely heavily inspired as a product by OpenClaw.”

Friedman, the former GitHub CEO who [joined Meta last year](https://time.com/collections/time100-ai-2025/7305854/alexandr-wang-and-nat-friedman/) alongside Meta’s Chief AI Officer [Alexandr Wang](https://www.meta.com/about/leadership/alexandr-wang/), said that the team at Meta had fallen in love with OpenClaw and wanted Muse to be “something like OpenClaw” that could be scaled to billions of people.

source_links.context: CaP-X uses [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management. Requires **Python 3.10** and a **CUDA-capable GPU**.

```
uv venv .venv-libero --python 3.12
source .venv-libero/bin/activate
uv sync --active --extra libero --extra contactgraspnet
```
See [docs/libero-tasks.md](https://github.com/capgym/cap-x/blob/main/docs/libero-tasks.md) for running any of 130+ LIBERO tasks.

```
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libegl1 libgl1
# Remove duplicate Vulkan ICD if present (causes segfault on multi-GPU systems)
sudo rm -f /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json
```
See [docs/behavior-tasks.md](https://github.com/capgym/cap-x/blob/main/docs/behavior-tasks.md) for task details and expected baselines.

**SAM3 authentication:** SAM3 weights require HuggingFace access. Request access at the [SAM3 repo](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3), then authenticate locally with `huggingface-cli login`. Weights are cached after first download.
See [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/capgym/cap-x/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) for all provider options (OpenRouter, vLLM, custom).
